plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do or believe, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks losses if you win at a price above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since values are private and independent, the optimal strategy is straightforward truth-telling: bid exactly my value of $25, ensuring maximum expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (given you win). Bidding above value risks winning and overpaying relative to value; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this holds regardless of competitors' strategies, the optimal action is straightforward truthful bidding. My value is $31, so I will bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This holds true even with rational opponents trying to anticipate my behavior - my optimal bid doesn't depend on their strategies. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own, so overbidding risks losing money and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $9.
